chunk_map.heading: # Prep the session, *fill the gaps* (H1 + lede)
Phase 1: Pick the task you'll send off
Push back until the task is one end-to-end slice
Phase 2: Walk your system against the task
Correct the list and reprioritise it
Fill the worst two or three gaps
Match each fill to its shape and home
Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase
Compare notes, then tidy the folder

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Since the last slides pin (d5aa7e3d) the only body change is the H1 rename, chunk 0 L1 'Prep the run' -> 'Prep the session, fill the gaps'; re-walked the whole sequential read against it. Chunk 0 L5's Session widget and L11 'Before the new session, check your working tree and branch' both resolve in-chunk ('the new session' = the widget two lines above) and now echo the new title rather than fighting it. Chunk 2 L34 'You'll use this task again next module' resolves to the scoped candidate from chunk 1. Chunk 3 L41 'the worst few gaps' resolves to chunk 0's L15 'the worst gaps' / L17 'the thin spots'. Chunk 5 L54 'not all five' resolves to chunk 3's 'ranked top-five' (L44). Chunk 6 L64 'the audit tags each gap with one' resolves to the Phase 2 audit named across chunk 3 (L40, L44). Chunk 6 L68 'not mid-send-off' - 'the send-off' is not named earlier in THIS file's body, but the enclosing module (`run-the-first-experiment.md`) names it in Prework (L14) and What You'll Learn (L23 '**Send off** the task un-packaged') ahead of this file's include (L39, itself now retitled 'Exercise: Prep the session, fill the gaps' in lockstep) - module include-order counts as prior context per the compendium's own clause, so this resolves. No referent left unnamed, vague-with-full-history, or stranded by the re-chunk.

No 'the opening lecture said' / 'as we saw earlier in [file]' shaped pointer anywhere in the body (unaffected by the title-only diff). Candidates touching other files: chunk 2 L34 and chunk 5 L54, both 'next module' - forward-pointing by relation, not a positional callback into another file's slide content. Chunk 6 L68's 'not mid-send-off' names the send-off by term (via the module's own signposting, rule 1), not by page position - satisfies the 'name it, don't locate it' carve-out.

Closest candidates are the two single-bullet chunks. Chunk 4 (L48-50): 'The ranking is Claude's read of your system. Tell it what's wrong, what's missing, and what you'd move up.' - a complete, actionable directive. Chunk 7 (L71-73): 'If Claude says something about your codebase you didn't tell it, ask where it read that.' - a self-carrying diagnostic-plus-action. Neither is a context-dependent wait-state fragment.

Chunk 0's new header 'Prep the session, *fill the gaps*' is answered by its own lede: L11 'Before the new session, check your working tree and branch' carries 'session', and L13-15's 'What you do'/'What you build' bullets carry 'fill the worst gaps' - no contradiction from the rename. Chunk 3 'Phase 2: Walk your system against the task' (L36) is answered almost verbatim by L40 'walk the system you have against the system the task needs.' Chunk 6 'Match each fill to its shape and home' (L62) is answered point-for-point by the four shape-to-destination bullets (L66-69). No header is contradicted by its chunk's content.

Ran `grep -nE "Not [A-Za-z].*\. Not [A-Za-z]"` on the body projection -> 0 hits. Ran `grep -niE "one of the (most|best)|the most (useful|important|valuable)"` on the body projection -> 0 hits (self-grading-superlative / value-prop-leak sub-item clean). Manual scan of all 9 chunks for anaphora/epistrophe triples: none. Numbers used ('one or two' L25, 'top-five'/'five' L40/L44, 'two or three, not all five' L54) are plain counts, none stated then walked back. No abstraction-noun stacks - language stays concrete ('observations/', 'CLAUDE.local.md', 'a connector', 'the Notion page'). No verb-triplet sentence with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget - bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 L25 bold 'Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than a big epic.' is the §34 task-sizing exception (whole-sentence bold mandated by §34, outranks §9) - confirmed against the maintainer accept-note at L84. Chunk 6 L66-69's four bolds ('Observation or rule:' / 'Sharpen an existing rule:' / 'Wire a connector:' / 'Bring the material in:') are a fill-shape menu, each <=4 words, matching the reading-list/menu waiver - confirmed by the maintainer accept-note at L90, which since d5aa7e3d was reworded to also name chunk 3's single 'Gap analysis' bold (L40) as sanctioned; the body's bold placement is unchanged, only the maintainer's description of it caught up. Chunk 3's 'Gap analysis' bold is one handle, inside the default <=1-per-slide budget. No other chunk carries any bold.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 8 `##` headings are imperative or phase-label form ('Phase 1: Pick the task you'll send off', 'Push back until the task is one end-to-end slice', 'Phase 2: Walk your system against the task', 'Correct the list and reprioritise it', 'Fill the worst two or three gaps', 'Match each fill to its shape and home', 'Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase', 'Compare notes, then tidy the folder'). None is a declarative law-statement; correct register for an exercise file, and this file is not one of the two declaratives the compendium's 2026-08-15 corpus measurement names.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies - three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every bullet against the three classes (doctrine restatement, self-referential design commentary, aphorism kicker). None found: L66-69 each name a distinct destination; L73 names a concrete diagnostic question. Closest candidates: L41 'Filling the worst few gaps is worth more than closing them all' and L54 'probably two or three, not all five' cover related ground, but the first states the prioritisation principle at the point Phase 2 introduces the audit and the second operationalises it into a concrete count at the point the student actually picks - a sequenced instruction, not a restatement. No self-referential design commentary or aphorism kicker anywhere in the body.
